title: Weather and Seasons
description: Expand your everyday vocabulary with weather words, seasonal expressions, and simple descriptions of climate. This course is designed for A1 completers who want to talk confidently about the weather and their seasonal preferences in English.

content.content: {"time":1700000001000,"blocks":[{"id":"aB1cD2eF3g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We use adjectives and nouns to describe the weather. Here are the most common words:"}},{"id":"hI4jK5lM6n","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["sunny — the sun is shining (e.g. It's a sunny day.)","cloudy — the sky is covered with clouds","rainy / it's raining — water falls from the sky","windy — there is a lot of wind","foggy — you cannot see far because of fog","stormy — there is a big storm with thunder and lightning"]}},{"id":"oP7qR8sT9u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We often say: It is + adjective → It is sunny. It is cold."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: It is a stormy day with thunder and lightning.

questions.text: The sky is dark and there is thunder. The weather is ___.
You cannot see the mountains because of thick mist. It is ___.
Which sentence is correct?

content.content: {"time":1700000002000,"blocks":[{"id":"vW0xY1zA2b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We use these words to talk about temperature:"}},{"id":"cD3eF4gH5i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["hot — very warm (30°C+)","warm — pleasantly heated (20–25°C)","cool — a little cold (10–15°C)","cold — low temperature (below 5°C)","freezing — extremely cold (below 0°C)"]}},{"id":"jK6lM7nO8p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We can also say: It is 20 degrees. or The temperature is minus five."}},{"id":"qR9sT0uV1w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Tip: In everyday English, people often combine two words: It's cold and windy today."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: It is freezing outside! The temperature is minus ten degrees.
It is [freezing] outside! Put on your coat. Last week the temperature was [minus] ten degrees. In summer it gets very [hot] — sometimes 35 degrees.

pairs.english: It is very cold and windy today.
The temperature is minus ten degrees.
It was warm and sunny yesterday.

questions.text: Which word means extremely cold (below 0°C)?

lessons.title: Describing Weather with 'It is' and 'There is'

content.content:
{"time":1700000003000,"blocks":[{"id":"xY2zA3bC4d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In English we use two main structures for weather descriptions:"}},{"id":"eF5gH6iJ7k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"It is + adjective:
It is sunny. / It is cold. / It is windy."}},{"id":"lM8nO9pQ0r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"There is/are + noun:
There is a storm. / There are dark clouds. / There is ice on the road."}},{"id":"sT1uV2wX3y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past tense: Use was/were:
It was rainy yesterday. / There was a big storm last night."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.targetPhrase: It was rainy yesterday and there was a big storm last night.

content.content: {"time":1700000004000,"blocks":[{"id":"zA4bC5dE6f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Spring comes after winter (March–May in the Northern Hemisphere). Key vocabulary:"}},{"id":"gH7iJ8kL9m","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["mild — not too hot, not too cold","blossom — flowers on a tree","shower — a short period of rain","muddy — wet and dirty ground","fresh — clean, cool air"]}},{"id":"nO0pQ1rS2t","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Example sentences: In spring the weather is mild and fresh. There are often short showers. Trees start to blossom."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

phrases.text: The weather is mild in spring.

guessItems.hint: Flowers that grow on a tree in spring
Not too hot, not too cold
Wet and dirty ground after rain

content.text: In spring the weather is mild and fresh. Trees start to blossom.
In [spring] the days get longer. The trees [blossom] and the air smells [fresh]. Sometimes there are short [showers], but it is usually [mild].

content.content: {"time":1700000005000,"blocks":[{"id":"uV3wX4yZ5a","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Summer is the hottest season (June–August). Useful vocabulary:"}},{"id":"bC6dE7fG8h","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["heatwave — a long period of very hot weather","humid — warm and wet air","thunderstorm — heavy rain with thunder and lightning","drought — a long time without rain","scorching — extremely hot"]}},{"id":"iJ9kL0mN1o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Common summer activities: going to the beach, swimming, having a barbecue, going on holiday."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Last summer was very hot and humid. There was a big thunderstorm last night.

content.content: {"time":1700000006000,"blocks":[{"id":"pQ2rS3tU4v","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Autumn (British English) / Fall (American English) is September–November. Vocabulary:"}},{"id":"wX5yZ6aB7c","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["crisp — cool and fresh (crisp autumn air)","overcast — the whole sky is grey and cloudy","drizzle — very light rain","breeze — a gentle wind","harvest — the time when crops are collected"]}},{"id":"dE8fG9hI0j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In autumn the leaves change color and fall from trees. The days become shorter and the nights longer."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: In autumn the sky is often overcast and grey. There is a cold breeze in the morning.
In autumn the sky is often [overcast] and grey. There is usually a cold [breeze] in the morning. Sometimes it [drizzles] all day. The days are shorter than in [summer].

content.content: {"time":1700000007000,"blocks":[{"id":"kL1mN2oP3q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Winter is December–February — the coldest season. Key vocabulary:"}},{"id":"rS4tU5vW6x","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["blizzard — a very bad snowstorm with strong wind","frost — a thin layer of ice on surfaces","slippery — easy to slip and fall (icy roads are slippery)","below zero — temperature under 0°C","snowfall — when snow falls from the sky"]}},{"id":"yZ7aB8cD9e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Winter activities: skiing, ice skating, building a snowman, drinking hot chocolate."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Be careful — the roads are slippery! It was below zero last night.

content.content: {"time":1700000008000,"blocks":[{"id":"fG0hI1jK2l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We can connect weather with activities using when and so:"}},{"id":"mN3oP4qR5s","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["When it is sunny, I go for a walk.","It was raining, so I stayed at home.","When it snowed, we went skiing."]}},{"id":"tU6vW7xY8z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Common weather-related phrases:"}},{"id":"aB9cD0eF1g","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["take an umbrella — carry an umbrella because it might rain","wrap up warm — wear warm clothes","stay indoors — stay inside the house","go out for a walk — leave the house to walk"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content: {"time":1700000009000,"blocks":[{"id":"hI2jK3lM4n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"To say what weather you like or dislike, use:"}},{"id":"oP5qR6sT7u","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["I love / like / enjoy + noun/verb-ing → I love sunny days. I enjoy skiing in the snow.","I don't like / I hate + noun/verb-ing → I hate rainy days. I don't like cold weather."]}},{"id":"vW8xY9zA0b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"To say what season you prefer:"}},{"id":"cD1eF2gH3i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["My favourite season is summer because it is warm and sunny.","I prefer winter because I like snow.","I don't enjoy autumn because it is often grey and cold."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: My favourite season is summer because I love sunny days and warm weather.

content.content: {"time":1700000010000,"blocks":[{"id":"jK4lM5nO6p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A weather forecast tells you what the weather will be like in the future. content.content: {"time":1700000011000,"blocks":[{"id":"eF3gH4iJ5k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Different parts of the world have different climates. A climate is the typical weather pattern in a region over a long time."}},{"id":"lM6nO7pQ8r","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["tropical climate — hot and humid all year (e.g. Brazil, Thailand)","desert climate — very hot and dry (e.g. Egypt, Australia's outback)","temperate climate — mild temperatures with four seasons (e.g. UK, France)","polar climate — very cold, snow and ice most of the year (e.g. Arctic, Antarctica)","mediterranean climate — warm, dry summers and mild, wet winters (e.g. Spain, Italy)"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}
